lanes.name: Ocean physics forecasting
lanes.workflow: Ingest dated ocean analyses and model-specific atmospheric forcing. Use GLONET as the default baseline for global forecasts and retain persistence as a low-cost reference.
lanes.protocol: Match initialization times, lead, variable, depth and wet-cell mask. Use OceanBench for the common global track. Score a separate native-resolution, sub-daily track for eddies and currents where observations resolve them.

lanes.name: Waves
lanes.workflow: Combine gridded wave state and weather forcing to forecast sea state. Match a station’s exposure and the model’s offshore grid before using a buoy for validation.
lanes.protocol: Hold out whole storms and stations. Score significant wave height in meters, period in seconds and direction using circular error. Match mean, peak and swell definitions before comparing.

lanes.name: Biogeochemistry
lanes.workflow: Forecast chemical or biological concentrations from gridded history and environmental drivers. Surface chlorophyll, dissolved oxygen, nutrients and carbon each need their own observations and units.
lanes.protocol: Match analyte, depth, basin, sampling interval and forecast lead. Compare against seasonal climatology and persistence on years excluded from fitting. Report errors by season and sampling coverage.

lanes.name: Satellite ocean color and radar
lanes.workflow: Prepare georeferenced satellite tiles. Optical ocean color uses spectral reflectance. Sentinel-1 radar measures backscatter and needs a separate preprocessing and evaluation workflow.
lanes.protocol: For optical chlorophyll retrieval, score field matchups by scene and region held out of training. Score bloom masks against annotated scenes. Evaluate radar embeddings only on a named radar task with matching labels.

lanes.name: Plankton imaging
lanes.workflow: Classify microscope crops and preserve instrument, sample time, crop identifier and sampled volume. In the Pioneer pilot, WHOI and PlankScope each produced a prediction for the same 24 images.
lanes.protocol: Use identical crops, an expert-reviewed label mapping and blind reference labels. Hold out water samples or deployments. Report group precision, recall, abstention and volume-normalized error with uncertainty.

lanes.name: Underwater imagery
lanes.workflow: Accept camera frames from dives or fixed stations for detection and segmentation. Pass cropped organisms to identification models. Above-water catch photographs form a separate test domain.
lanes.protocol: Hold out dives, sites and camera systems. Score boxes with average precision, masks with intersection over union and crop classification with macro recall. Match annotation classes and background policy before scoring two detectors.

lanes.name: Coral reefs
lanes.workflow: Segment coral in underwater photographs or transect frames. Keep masks, expert-assigned groups and the area denominator together when estimating cover.
lanes.protocol: Hold out reefs or transects. Compare binary masks on the same valid pixels, then report error in coral cover as percentage points. Species-level tests require separate reference labels.

lanes.name: Bioacoustics
lanes.workflow: Process hydrophone recordings with their sample rate, station, time and duty cycle. Train a small supervised classifier on embeddings when a target sound has no released detector.
lanes.protocol: Compare models on the same species, call type, frequency band and time window. Hold out recorder-days or sites. Report event recall at a fixed false-alarm rate per recording hour and separate clip-level scores.

lanes.name: Language and scientific Q&A
lanes.workflow: Give each language model the same approved measurements, data-quality flags and retrieved sources. Evaluate text questions separately from interpretation of sonar or microscope imagery.
lanes.protocol: Pin the model version and evidence packet. Grade numerical accuracy, citation support and abstention on missing evidence. Blind reviewers to model identity and record latency, GPU memory or API cost.

models.name: GLONET
models.task: Generate short-range global ocean physics forecasts.
models.input: Two days of initial physical ocean fields. The released workflow retrieves Copernicus Marine initialization and regrids it. The paper trained on GLORYS12.
models.output: Ten daily global maps of sea surface height and temperature, salinity and horizontal currents on a 1/4° output grid with 21 depth levels.
models.compute: The official inference card requires an NVIDIA GPU and reports a ten-day forecast in seconds. Training used multi-GPU pipeline parallelism. Download, regridding and output I/O add elapsed time. L40S performance has not been measured here.
models.access: Mercator publishes three depth-specific TorchScript weight files, normalization statistics and inference code. Copernicus Marine credentials are required by its data-fetching workflow.
models.license: EUPL-1.2 for code. CC BY 4.0 for weights and associated statistics.
models.benchmark: Use its OceanBench GLO12-initialized 2024 challenger scores against GLO12 and persistence on the same track and grid. Extract wet grid cells around Pioneer and compare against matched station temperature, salinity and currents.
models.notes: The card distinguishes its 1/4° output grid from an author-described 1/12° effective resolution. Use the actual output grid for coastal collocation.

models.name: FuXi-Ocean
models.task: Forecast sub-daily global ocean physics and storm responses.
models.input: Four historical six-hour states with HYCOM ocean fields and five near-surface atmospheric variables. ERA5 supplied atmospheric training inputs. The rollout needs no future atmospheric forecast.
models.output: Six-hourly 1/12° temperature, salinity and horizontal currents on 26 levels to 1,500 m, plus sea surface height, through ten days.
models.compute: Authors report 72 seconds for a ten-day global forecast on one H100. This is inference. Local peak memory and L40S runtime are unverified.
models.access: The authors’ DOI archive contains a README, requirements and two inference scripts. The inference script expects an external ONNX file. The author GitHub tree also provides scripts. A publicly downloadable author-trained checkpoint was not verified.
models.license: CC BY 4.0 on the cited Zenodo deposit. A license for the missing trained weights is unverified.
models.benchmark: The paper tested 2022 forecasts against HYCOM, OceanMAPS, FOAM and WenHai with satellite and in-situ reference data, including profiles and currents. The paper averaged FuXi-Ocean output to daily means for daily comparisons. These are separate from Mercator’s 2024 OceanBench scores.
models.notes: Author code: https://github.com/huangqiusheng/FuXi-Ocean. The OneScience-Group engineering reproduction describes synthetic training tiles and disclaims original weights (https://huggingface.co/OneScience-Group/FuXi-Ocean).

models.name: WenHai
models.task: Forecast the eddying upper ocean with physically calculated air–sea fluxes and a Swin Transformer.
models.input: Five initial ocean variables, plus eight surface atmospheric variables to calculate fluxes. Training used GLORYS and ERA5. The operational-style comparison used GLO12 initialization and IFS atmospheric forecasts.
models.output: Daily 1/12° sea surface height and temperature, salinity and horizontal currents on 23 vertical levels down to about 644 m.
models.compute: The paper describes a high-resolution training stage exceeding 80 GB of GPU memory before distributing layers across devices. The author supplies ONNX inference code. Peak inference memory and L40S latency are unverified.
models.access: The author repository links the WenHai.onnx weights, example inputs, masks and normalization arrays in Google Drive. The public folder lists the weight file.
models.license: The v1.0 archived GitHub source release is marked CC BY 4.0 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14881628). The ONNX file is delivered separately. Its license was not verified.
models.benchmark: The authors compared with GLO12v4 under matched initialization and forcing in April–November 2024. OceanBench hosts a common 2024 comparison with XiHe, GLONET and persistence. Score station errors by depth and forecast lead.
models.notes: The released GLORYS mask differs from the GLO12 mask. Check grid and wet-cell consistency before matching Pioneer observations.

models.name: XiHe
models.task: Predict global eddy-resolving ocean physics at fixed leads.
models.input: Initial ocean state and 10 m zonal/meridional wind. The original work trained on GLORYS12 and ERA5. The OceanBench challenger used GLO12/IFS.
models.output: Global 1/12° temperature, salinity and horizontal currents on 23 levels down to about 644 m, with sea surface height and surface temperature. The released ONNX collection covers lead days one to ten.
models.compute: The revised paper reports 0.35 s on one GPU for a day-ten prediction. The release supplies lead-specific models. This timing does not establish end-to-end latency for all ten leads, input preparation or local deployment.
models.access: The author repository links pretrained upper/deeper ONNX files for each forecast lead via Google Drive and Baidu mirrors.
models.license: No explicit repository or model-weight reuse license was verified. The arXiv paper’s distribution terms apply to the manuscript.
models.benchmark: The paper uses 2019–2020 satellite/in-situ verification and the IV-TT Class 4 framework. Use the separate OceanBench 2024 run for a like-for-like comparison with GLONET and WenHai.
models.notes: Archive the chosen lead, depth partition and exact checkpoint before attributing a forecast to XiHe.

models.name: OceanBench (Mercator Ocean International)
models.task: Evaluate global ocean physics forecasts using a common verification protocol.
models.input: Ten-day forecasts initialized on all 52 Wednesdays of 2024. The framework accepts 1/12°, 1/4° and 1° grids and documents the variable, depth and coordinate conventions.
models.output: Scores by lead, variable and depth, matched-observation counts, gridded scores and physical diagnostics.
models.compute: Scores can be read from the hosted leaderboard. Re-scoring uses the Python package and reference data. Copernicus Marine sign-in is required for 1/12° evaluations. A forecast-model GPU training budget does not apply.
models.access: Public evaluation code, methods and scores. OceanBench provides no prediction weights of its own.
models.license: EUPL-1.2 for the evaluation project. Reference and challenger datasets carry their providers’ terms.
models.benchmark: Compare challengers against GLORYS reanalysis, GLO12 analysis and matched Argo profiles, surface drifters and along-track altimetry. Keep the reference, mask, track, version and grid fixed. Class IV coastal masking excludes some nearshore observations.
models.notes: NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks. The live roster includes GLONET, WenHai and XiHe. FuXi-Ocean does not appear on this roster. Check the roster (https://oceanbench.edito.eu/challengers/) and verification definitions (https://oceanbench.edito.eu/evaluation-methods/) for each comparison. Perform separate station-scale validation at Pioneer.

models.name: Aurora 0.25° Wave
models.task: Forecast global ocean surface waves and atmospheric conditions.
models.input: Two six-hourly global states of HRES T0 weather and HRES-WAM wave analysis, 13 atmospheric pressure levels and static fields including the wave mask. Required channels and initialization are specified by Microsoft.
models.output: Six-hourly wave fields on a 1/4° grid, including significant wave height, mean direction, periods, wind waves and swell partitions. The paper evaluated horizons to ten days.
models.compute: The published wave checkpoint is 5.04 GB on disk. The paper reports 32 A100s for foundation-model pretraining. Weight size is only one component of inference memory. Wave inference on this L40S has not been timed.
models.access: Microsoft publishes aurora-0.25-wave.ckpt and wave static data. Its documentation includes an inference example. Historical HRES T0 and HRES-WAM archive access must be checked separately.
models.license: MIT for the published model repository and Microsoft’s Aurora implementation. ECMWF input datasets are governed by separate terms.
models.benchmark: The Nature study compares against ECMWF HRES-WAM. For Pioneer, collocate significant wave height in metres with quality-controlled OOI or NDBC buoy observations and compare errors to persistence or archived wave guidance at identical valid times. Evaluate directions using circular error.
models.notes: This is the wave-specific checkpoint, distinct from the atmospheric Aurora checkpoints. Input contract: https://microsoft.github.io/aurora/models.html. Example: https://microsoft.github.io/aurora/example_wave.html.

models.name: Mercator seasonal surface chlorophyll-a U-Net (Martinez Balbontin et al.)
models.task: Estimate near-global surface chlorophyll-a from physical drivers and produce seasonal forecasts.
models.input: Mixed-layer depth, sea surface height, sea surface salinity and temperature. Training paired GLORYS12 with GlobColour observations. Seasonal forecasts use bias-adjusted ECMWF SEAS5 predictors.
models.output: Surface chlorophyll-a on a 1/4° near-global grid. The seasonal experiment produces monthly forecasts to six months. A separate reconstruction experiment uses five-day averages.
models.compute: Authors trained on one 40 GB A100 and report training in hours and six months of forecast maps in minutes on a single GPU, conditional on having the physical forecasts. This has not been replicated on the L40S.
models.access: The paper offers software by request from the corresponding author. A public pretrained checkpoint or release was not verified.
models.license: The article is CC BY 4.0. Code/weights redistribution terms were not verified. The paper identifies the licenses/providers for source data separately.
models.benchmark: Validate against GlobColour. The paper evaluated five-day reconstructions over 2018–2023 and monthly seasonal forecasts over 2020–2023, with BIO4 as a contextual comparison. For Pioneer, score surface chlorophyll against seasonal climatology; measure taxon concentrations separately using IFCB.
models.notes: The authors used higher-resolution SEAS5 supplied by ECMWF. Public monthly SEAS5 inputs are 1° and require interpolation for the 1/4° workflow. Surface chlorophyll alone cannot identify plankton or recover a subsurface chlorophyll maximum.

models.name: BG4Sea
models.task: Emulate and forecast seasonal three-dimensional marine biogeochemistry.
models.input: Monthly BIORYS4 NEMO/PISCES biogeochemical columns and GLORYS12 physical fields. The authors compare column-only, surface-conditioned and spatially coupled configurations.
models.output: Monthly 1/4° forecasts to six months. The full state comprises 29 biogeochemical variables plus temperature and salinity at 24 depths, including nutrients, oxygen, carbon pools and plankton variables.
models.compute: The authors describe a compressed, progressively coupled architecture. A comparable GPU runtime, peak memory or L40S benchmark was not verified. The earlier chlorophyll U-Net timing is a different experiment.
models.access: Author preprint, Mercator project summary and EGU 2026 abstract are public. A public code or pretrained-weight release was not verified.
models.license: The preprint and EGU presentation document scientific work. Model code/weights reuse terms were not verified.
models.benchmark: Tested against BIORYS4 for 2020–2022, with persistence and climatology baselines. Seasonal skill against a numerical analysis needs a separate test against measured nutrients, oxygen or chlorophyll at Pioneer, grouped by lead and depth.
models.notes: Mercator reported a NeurIPS@Cam community poster award in December 2025 (https://www.mercator-ocean.eu/news-en/bg4sea-ai-forecasting/). There is an EGU 2026 contribution (https://meetingorganizer.copernicus.org/EGU26/EGU26-13007.html) and a July 2026 author preprint. A NeurIPS 2026 main-conference listing was not verified in the program (https://neurips.cc/Downloads/2026).

models.name: NASA MODIS OC3M (R2022 band-ratio component)
models.task: Estimate near-surface chlorophyll-a from a single MODIS ocean-color pixel.
models.input: Atmosphere-corrected remote-sensing reflectance (sr⁻¹) at 443, 488 and 547 nm from the same water pixel.
models.output: Estimated chlorophyll-a (mg/m³), selected blue band and blue-to-green ratio.
models.compute: Deterministic polynomial evaluated on the browser CPU; no GPU or network service required.
models.access: Runnable browser model with published coefficients. No learned weight download or account is required.
models.license: NASA publishes the coefficients and describes unrestricted chlor_a product usage. Cite the ATBD and sensor collection for observed reflectances.
models.benchmark: Use SeaBASS pigment matchups with pixel flags and explicit space/time windows, report log error, bias and retained observations on held-out scenes. The operational color-index blend is a separate comparator.
models.notes: R2022 coefficients documented 6 November 2023, Table 1. The demonstration starts with illustrative reflectances. NASA’s blended chlor_a product also uses a color-index retrieval.

models.name: NASA Ocean Color chlor_a (OCI/OCx blend)
models.task: Retrieve near-surface chlorophyll-a as an optical baseline.
models.input: Quality-screened water-leaving remote-sensing reflectance in sensor-specific blue, green and red bands.
models.output: Chlorophyll-a in mg/m³ per valid pixel.
models.compute: Published per-pixel algebraic retrieval. Proposed CPU processing of local granules; local time unmeasured.
models.access: Public standard product and algorithm description; no network weights.
models.license: NASA Earth science data policy applies to the mission product; cite collection and reprocessing version.
models.benchmark: Compare against colocated extracted chlorophyll in SeaBASS; report log error, bias and retained matchup count, including cloud gaps.
models.notes: NASA’s November 2023 ATBD documents reprocessing R2022. In situ fluorometry requires its own calibration. Species composition is outside this product's scope.

models.name: NASA PACE OCI MOANA
models.task: Estimate three picophytoplankton groups at the Atlantic surface.
models.input: Hyperspectral ocean-color reflectance and sea-surface temperature; the NASA tutorial uses 4 km gridded outputs.
models.output: Abundance in cells/mL for Prochlorococcus, Synechococcus and autotrophic picoeukaryotes.
models.compute: Published gridded retrieval; proposed CPU subsetting of daily fields. Local compute unmeasured.
models.access: Public NASA Level-4 MOANA data product. NASA Earthdata Login supports download; no checkpoint needed.
models.license: NASA Earth science data policy covers the distributed product; cite its versioned DOI.
models.benchmark: Validate against simultaneous near-surface flow-cytometry measurements of the same groups, with withheld cruises; record coverage, bias and error for each.
models.notes: 2020 algorithm; NASA documents product v3.2. Its target organisms are <2 µm. Pioneer IFCB ROI counts at 7 m cannot directly validate these three cell concentrations.

models.name: IBM Granite Geospatial Ocean
models.task: Encode optical ocean patches and fit a task head for chlorophyll-a or primary production.
models.input: 42×42 patches with 16 Sentinel-3 OLCI Level-2 bands; pretraining also used collocated SLSTR sea-surface temperature.
models.output: Patch representations; a separately fitted regression head estimates the target field.
models.compute: Published checkpoint 166 MB; IBM's fine-tuning tutorial recommends a T4. Proposed L40S patch inference; local memory/time unmeasured.
models.access: Public TerraTorch backbone checkpoint; tutorial includes a primary-production fine-tuning example.
models.license: Apache-2.0 model repository; Sentinel inputs and field reference data carry their own terms.
models.benchmark: Paper used five random folds on 188 chlorophyll and 103 production observations. Repeat with held-out cruises and compare to Level-2 retrieval, ExtraTrees and a randomly initialized model.
models.notes: September 2025 preprint. Five-fold chlorophyll RMSE was similar across the learned baselines. A matching sensor stack and independent local labels are needed for a Pioneer test.

models.name: OceanSAR-2
models.task: Extract ocean-surface radar features for wind, wave height and geophysical pattern probes.
models.input: Radiometrically calibrated Sentinel-1 Wave Mode SAR backscatter (σ⁰).
models.output: Image/patch embeddings; a separate probe or head produces a geophysical prediction.
models.compute: Paper reports 21M parameters. L40S time/memory unmeasured; local inference depends on weights.
models.access: Paper and benchmark definitions public. No v2 checkpoint verified in the authors' public Hugging Face model list.
models.license: V2 weight license unverified; the paper license and OceanSAR-1 terms do not establish v2 weight rights.
models.benchmark: Paper k-nearest-neighbors benchmark: TenGeoP accuracy 94.0%, significant wave height RMSE 0.52 m, wind-speed RMSE 1.32 m/s. Use matched buoy observations for a local test.
models.notes: January 2026. Sentinel-1 radar measures surface texture. Where appropriate wave-mode scenes overlap the event, it can add storm context to a replay.

models.name: OceanSAR-1-wave (ResNet-50)
models.task: Estimate significant wave height from radar as a runnable storm comparator.
models.input: Sentinel-1 Wave Mode radar tiles using the v1 processor and normalization.
models.output: Significant wave height in meters.
models.compute: Public ResNet-50 model and linear head, ~23.6M parameters. Proposed single-GPU tile run; no local timings.
models.access: Public checkpoint and image processor on the authors’ Hugging Face repository; load via the documented Transformers interface.
models.license: Apache-2.0 for this released model; source radar and ground observations have separate terms.
models.benchmark: Model card reports 0.63 m wave-height RMSE for this specific backbone. Measure RMSE and bias against time/space-matched buoy SWH, stratified by sea state.
models.notes: April 2025. Keep the v1 preprocessing and v1 benchmark with this release; several ViT results in the card refer to other backbones.

models.name: WHOI Northeast Shelf IFCB v2.4
models.task: Classify microscope crops of plankton, nonliving particles and imaging artifacts.
models.input: Individual grayscale IFCB ROI, resized to 299×299, repeated into three channels, scaled to [0,1].
models.output: Logits for 155 categories; downstream softmax and top-three suggestions.
models.compute: Public ONNX ~85 MB. A local CPU processed 24 Pioneer originals; GPU speed and full-event throughput unmeasured.
models.access: Public frozen Inception V3 ONNX model, label list and preprocessing.
models.license: MIT model weights; the separate WHOI 97,026-image reference dataset is CC BY 4.0.
models.benchmark: WHOI reports macro-F1 0.9191 on its validation split. Our 24 crops test compatibility. Compare to the blind, date-held-out Pioneer broad-group audit.
models.notes: 2022 classifier, Inception V3. A softmax score needs local calibration. Multiple organisms or a chain can share one crop.

models.name: SIG.AI PlankScope crop classifier
models.task: Classify individual microscope crops and compare suggestions across cameras on identical original images.
models.input: An individual original microscope ROI with model-specific preprocessing.
models.output: Ranked candidates from a 101-class ResNet-50. Instrument CSV comparisons use the top suggestion and score.
models.compute: Direct crop inference ran on the NVIDIA L40S behind the signed-in OOI Jupyter widget. The public CSV comparison runs locally in the browser.
models.access: Authorized users can run the private classifier through the plankton identification notebook in OOI. The public trial accepts exported predictions and pairs them with WHOI results by image checksum.
models.license: No public weight or redistribution license verified. Public comparison instructions cover the interface.
models.benchmark: Compare the same SHA-256-matched crops by expert-mapped ecological group; measure coverage, precision and recall against withheld human labels. Report model agreement separately.
models.notes: The public adapter contains inference code. Model weights and the ordered class map remain private. A 24-crop pilot established cross-camera input compatibility; independent expert labels are needed for Pioneer accuracy.

models.name: MobileNetV2 + MLP₆₀₀ (plankton benchmark)
models.task: Train a lightweight plankton image classifier per instrument.
models.input: Single grayscale ROI with aspect-preserving resize, border-median padding to 224×224 and three identical channels.
models.output: Per-instrument class scores after training a 600-unit hidden layer and classification head.
models.compute: Published: ten epochs took 15 h for IFCB and 5 h for ISIIS on a Quadro RTX 8000. Proposed L40S pilot; benchmark time is hardware- and dataset-specific.
models.access: Public training and evaluation code, original test metrics and dataset links. Trained plankton checkpoints were not present in the v1.0.2 archive.
models.license: Zenodo software snapshot specifies CC BY 4.0. Each source dataset has its own license.
models.benchmark: Authors report balanced accuracy of 79–90% across six imaging datasets. Compare a newly trained IFCB model to WHOI on the same independently adjudicated Pioneer sample.
models.notes: 2026 paper, December 2025 code archive. Published source-specific classifiers used ImageNet initialization and per-class weighting. Generic ImageNet weights alone do not classify plankton taxa.

models.name: Planktonzilla EVA02-Large (supervised)
models.task: Assign a fixed taxon lineage to a microscope or plankton-imager crop.
models.input: 3×448×448 image using the card's bicubic squash and normalization.
models.output: Single-label scores over 385 taxonomic lineages.
models.compute: Published checkpoint ~1.22 GB, ~0.3B parameters. Proposed batch-one L40S inference; local usage unmeasured.
models.access: Model card public; actual safetensors download requires approved Hugging Face access.
models.license: MIT tag on this checkpoint. The separate Planktonzilla-17M image collection aggregates multiple licenses.
models.benchmark: Model card validation top-1 0.9499 and macro-F1 0.8861. Blind-test IFCB with lineage-to-group mapping and report coverage, especially debris.
models.notes: May 2026 paper. The checkpoint was trained on the plankton subset. Its 385 labels differ from the larger dataset inventory.

models.name: Planktonzilla CLIP ViT-B/16 (OpenAI)
models.task: Rank candidate taxonomic lineages and retrieve similar images.
models.input: 224×224 plankton image and text describing candidate taxonomic lineages.
models.output: Image/text embeddings (512 dimensions) and relative image–text similarity scores.
models.compute: Checkpoint ~0.60 GB. Published CLIP training used 64 H100s over 100 epochs. Proposed frozen L40S inference; local throughput unmeasured.
models.access: Public model card. The packaged OpenCLIP safetensors require approved Hugging Face access.
models.license: MIT tag on this model card. Source images in Planktonzilla-17M retain their individual licenses.
models.benchmark: Published in-domain macro-F1: genus 0.797, species 0.786. Evaluate held-out imagers or dates with fixed candidate prompts; report coverage at each rank.
models.notes: May 2026 paper. Initialization: OpenAI. Explicitly test non-plankton and unfamiliar taxa; a similarity ranking cannot certify species identity.

models.name: Planktonzilla CLIP ViT-B/16 (BioCLIP)
models.task: Rank candidate taxonomic lineages and retrieve similar images.
models.input: 224×224 plankton image and text describing candidate taxonomic lineages.
models.output: Image/text embeddings (512 dimensions) and relative image–text similarity scores.
models.compute: Checkpoint ~0.60 GB. Published CLIP training used 64 H100s over 100 epochs. Proposed frozen L40S inference; local throughput unmeasured.
models.access: Public model card. The packaged OpenCLIP safetensors require approved Hugging Face access.
models.license: MIT tag on this model card. Source images in Planktonzilla-17M retain their individual licenses.
models.benchmark: Published in-domain macro-F1: genus 0.752, species 0.734. Evaluate held-out imagers or dates with fixed candidate prompts; report coverage at each rank.
models.notes: May 2026 paper. Initialization: BioCLIP. Explicitly test non-plankton and unfamiliar taxa; a similarity ranking cannot certify species identity.

models.name: Planktonzilla CLIP ViT-L/14 (LAION-2B)
models.task: Rank candidate taxonomic lineages and retrieve similar images.
models.input: 224×224 plankton image and text describing candidate taxonomic lineages.
models.output: Image/text embeddings (768 dimensions) and relative image–text similarity scores.
models.compute: Checkpoint ~1.71 GB. Published CLIP training used 64 H100s over 100 epochs. Proposed frozen L40S inference; local throughput unmeasured.
models.access: Public model card. The packaged OpenCLIP safetensors require approved Hugging Face access.
models.license: MIT tag on this model card. Source images in Planktonzilla-17M retain their individual licenses.
models.benchmark: Published in-domain macro-F1: genus 0.839, species 0.825. Evaluate held-out imagers or dates with fixed candidate prompts; report coverage at each rank.
models.notes: May 2026 paper. Initialization: LAION-2B. Explicitly test non-plankton and unfamiliar taxa; a similarity ranking cannot certify species identity.

models.name: Planktonzilla CLIP ViT-L/14 (BioCLIP 2)
models.task: Rank candidate taxonomic lineages and retrieve similar images.
models.input: 224×224 plankton image and text describing candidate taxonomic lineages.
models.output: Image/text embeddings (768 dimensions) and relative image–text similarity scores.
models.compute: Checkpoint ~1.71 GB. Published CLIP training used 64 H100s over 100 epochs. Proposed frozen L40S inference; local throughput unmeasured.
models.access: Public model card. The packaged OpenCLIP safetensors require approved Hugging Face access.
models.license: MIT tag on this model card. Source images in Planktonzilla-17M retain their individual licenses.
models.benchmark: Published in-domain macro-F1: genus 0.823, species 0.816. Evaluate held-out imagers or dates with fixed candidate prompts; report coverage at each rank.
models.notes: May 2026 paper. Initialization: BioCLIP 2. Explicitly test non-plankton and unfamiliar taxa; a similarity ranking cannot certify species identity.

models.name: SIG.AI ten-class IFCB morphology baseline
models.task: Classify a single microscope crop using native particle size, shape and grayscale statistics.
models.input: One original grayscale IFCB crop at its native resolution. The estimator uses 20 features of dimensions, intensity and silhouette.
models.output: Ten class distances and the nearest class centroid. A smaller standardized distance indicates a closer match.
models.compute: The fitted JSON parameter file is about 9.4 kB. The browser computes the features and centroid distances on its CPU.
models.access: Public fitted centroids, feature scales and browser inference. The repository includes a reproducible training script.
models.license: WHOI training images are CC BY 4.0. The project has not specified a separate license for the fitted baseline parameters.
models.benchmark: On the ten-label WHOI pilot, 131/250 correct (52.4%), macro-F1 0.5068. Compare with MobileNetV3 on these same 250 crops from 211 held-out bins.
models.notes: Fit on 1,280 expert-labeled WHOI images. Native pixel dimensions are features, so rescaling inputs can change predictions. Independent Pioneer accuracy remains unmeasured.

models.name: SIG.AI ten-class IFCB MobileNetV3-Small
models.task: Fit a supervised ten-class head on frozen image features and classify an individual IFCB crop.
models.input: One grayscale WHOI or IFCB image, aspect-preserving resize with padding to 224×224, replicated RGB, ImageNet normalization.
models.output: Ten class scores and ranked candidates. The training notebook exports the fitted model, validation predictions and a personal ONNX file.
models.compute: Training and inference ran on the OOI NVIDIA L40S. An independent CPU fit reproduced its held-out accuracy and macro-F1. The personal ONNX export runs on the user’s device.
models.access: The signed-in notebook runs the fitted model and exports a personal ONNX file. The public browser trial accepts the file and its SHA-256 and checks the hash before inference.
models.license: WHOI training images are CC BY 4.0. TorchVision's code uses BSD-3-Clause; upstream ImageNet weights and the locally fitted head have separate scope. No separate redistribution license was identified for the fitted head.
models.benchmark: OOI L40S: 221/250 correct (88.4%), macro-F1 0.88446 across 211 held-out bins. The exported ONNX model reproduced the PyTorch top label on all 250 crops. On this split, the majority-class baseline achieved 10% accuracy.
models.notes: 1,280 training crops from 989 bins. Ten labels have equal representation in this pilot. Natural abundance and performance on independent Pioneer events require separate evaluation.

models.name: PML IFCB CLIP-LoRA (145 classes)
models.task: Rank microscope crops against visual or textual references with a single adapted image encoder.
models.input: One IFCB specimen crop. The CLIP transform resizes and center-crops to 224×224 RGB. Choose image class means or taxonomic lineage text prototypes.
models.output: Ranked matches among the same 145 PML reference classes, with cosine similarity scores.
models.compute: Pinned downloads include a 598.5 MB ViT-B/16 base and a 16.4 MB adapter and prototype bundle. The identification notebook ran this model on the OOI NVIDIA L40S.
models.access: Public adapter, label map and both prototype banks. The pinned base checkpoint is downloaded separately. A workspace notebook runs the two modes.
models.license: Author model card specifies MIT for the adapter package. The pinned timm base checkpoint card specifies Apache-2.0. Training image collections have separate terms.
models.benchmark: Author’s 14,837-image PML IFCB test: image prototypes reached 0.773 accuracy and 0.636 macro-F1; text prototypes reached 0.282 and 0.145. Score modes on identical crops and aligned labels.
models.notes: One CLIP-LoRA encoder powers both ranking modes. The DINOv3 classifier described on the same model card is a separate checkpoint. The quoted scores apply to PML.

models.name: FathomNet Megalodon (2024 YOLO11x)
models.task: Localize salient underwater objects.
models.input: Underwater still images or individual video frames.
models.output: Bounding boxes and detection scores for one generic object class.
models.compute: Ultralytics YOLO11x; propose L40S batched inference and measure frames/s.
models.access: Public PyTorch weights on the FathomNet model hub. Earlier YOLOv8x checkpoint also published.
models.license: Checkpoint labeled CC BY 4.0. Runtime and source imagery have separate terms.
models.benchmark: Score class-agnostic AP50:95 and recall on FathomNet/2024-megalodon-benchmark and on expert-boxed OOI frames from a held-out deployment.
models.notes: Useful for generating crops. Species recognition requires a separate classifier. Official benchmark https://huggingface.co/datasets/FathomNet/2024-megalodon-benchmark

models.name: FathomNet vulnerable marine ecosystems detector
models.task: Detect four broad groups in deep-sea benthic images.
models.input: Seafloor camera images or video frames.
models.output: Boxes, scores and categories for coral, crinoid, sponge and fish.
models.compute: Ultralytics YOLOv8x; propose single-GPU inference.
models.access: Public best.pt checkpoint in FathomNet repository.
models.license: Model card labels checkpoint CC BY 4.0. Source imagery and runtime have separate terms.
models.benchmark: Compare per-group box AP and missed animals on FathomNet/2024-vme-benchmark and an independent OOI camera-day sample.
models.notes: Thresholds and lighting can change precision substantially. The presence of one detected animal does not establish a legal VME designation. Benchmark https://huggingface.co/datasets/FathomNet/2024-vme-benchmark

models.name: Southern Hydrate Ridge digital still camera YOLO model
models.task: OOI-specific baseline for visible seafloor fauna.
models.input: Frames from the OOI Southern Hydrate Ridge still camera.
models.output: Bounding boxes and scores in 12 categories, including sablefish, sea stars, sea anemones, and clams.
models.compute: Public YOLO model; propose single L40S inference, benchmark memory and frames/s.
models.access: Creator publishes downloadable best.pt weights, about 137 MB.
models.license: MIT on the model card. Check underlying imagery and runtime terms separately.
models.benchmark: Hold out later deployments or camera days, check training overlap, and measure per-category box AP and false positives on empty images.
models.notes: The author reports rockfish and vesicomyid clams were overrepresented. Camera owner https://interactiveoceans.washington.edu/research-sites/southern-hydrate-ridge/

models.name: BioCLIP 2 (ViT-L/14)
models.task: Classify or retrieve organism crops by taxonomic text or labeled examples.
models.input: Organism image and candidate taxonomic descriptions, or a labeled reference gallery.
models.output: Image and text embeddings, similarity ranks, or downstream classification scores.
models.compute: Authors list 428M parameters and about 1.7 GB FP32 weights. Profile complete L40S runtime independently.
models.access: Public OpenCLIP weights in Safetensors and PyTorch formats.
models.license: Checkpoint card declares MIT. Images in TreeOfLife-200M retain source-specific terms.
models.benchmark: Compare zero-shot or fixed-budget linear probes with BioCLIP 2.5 on identical fish crops, vocabulary and dive-level splits. Report top-k, macro-F1 and unknown rejection.
models.notes: FishNet in the authors' evaluation tests ecological traits/habitat. A separate site-labeled test is needed for underwater species identification.

models.name: BioCLIP 2.5 Huge (ViT-H/14)
models.task: Compare a larger biological image encoder for identification and ecological traits.
models.input: Organism crop and taxonomic labels/prompts, or expert-labeled training examples.
models.output: Embedding similarities, taxon ranks, or supervised probe predictions.
models.compute: Authors list 986M parameters and about 3.9 GB FP32 weights. Batch sizing and latency on the L40S are proposed tests.
models.access: Public OpenCLIP weights in Safetensors and PyTorch formats.
models.license: MIT on the checkpoint card. Training-image rights vary by source.
models.benchmark: Authors include FishNet habitat/trait evaluation. Compare against BioCLIP 2 on equal expert-labeled crops; assess abstention, latency and held-out camera performance.
models.notes: Works on crops and candidate names; pair with Megalodon or reviewed boxes for whole-frame detection.

models.name: Fishial.ai fish identification (v0.10.2)
models.task: Recognize fish in photographs; project also distributes fish detection and segmentation models.
models.input: Fish crop for the classifier; upstream detector/segmenter accepts a full photograph.
models.output: 768-dimensional DINOv2-derived embedding with class-reference matches across 866 classes for this checkpoint.
models.compute: Official project supplies TorchScript and Colab. Propose CPU smoke test and L40S crop batches.
models.access: Official repo links downloadable TorchScript classifier v0.10.2 and separate detector and segmentation packs; hosted API is an alternative.
models.license: Repository declares MIT for the project. Confirm separate model-archive and original-photo terms for redistribution.
models.benchmark: Run Fishial and BioCLIP on the same reviewed fish crops with common covered taxa. Measure top-k accuracy, macro-recall, unsupported taxa and camera-domain shift. Evaluate detector misses separately.
models.notes: Version the checkpoint label file. The hosted Fishial API and other public releases have different species counts.

models.name: CoralSCOP ViT-B
models.task: Segment individual coral in underwater reef survey photographs.
models.input: Underwater RGB reef photograph; optional point or box prompts under the evaluated settings.
models.output: Instance masks; mask area can estimate image-plane coral cover after validation.
models.compute: Paper pretraining used six A100 GPUs for five epochs. Author demo supports one GPU. Proposed L40S image-at-a-time inference, unmeasured.
models.access: Authors released ViT-B weights via the official repository's download link and published inference code.
models.license: Author repository LICENSE.txt is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. No separate broader weight rights verified. Survey images need their own terms.
models.benchmark: Paper Table 1 mask IoU: 59.02% automatic, 62.90% with one point, 74.00% with point and box. Compare with SAM and independently drawn masks on held-out reefs.
models.notes: CVPR 2024, author weights announced 28 September 2024. Use benthic survey photos for this lane. Required image geometry and outputs differ from IFCB crops.

models.name: Perch 2.0
models.task: Transfer a general bioacoustic encoder to passive marine recordings.
models.input: Five-second mono waveforms at 32 kHz.
models.output: 1,536-dimensional embeddings and pretrained logits. Fit a local probe for underwater event labels.
models.compute: Google's standard TF2 variant requires TensorFlow ≥2.20 and a GPU. A separate CPU checkpoint exists. Profile L40S compatibility.
models.access: Public Google TensorFlow SavedModel on Kaggle, with GPU and CPU variants.
models.license: Apache 2.0 on Google’s Kaggle model variants. Source audio has separate terms.
models.benchmark: Compare equal-budget frozen-embedding probes against SurfPerch and the whale model on shared labels. Split by site, recorder and date. Use PR-AUC and false alarms/hour; account for pretraining overlap.
models.notes: The source study tests underwater transfer. General-purpose BEANS includes marine mammals https://github.com/earthspecies/beans

models.name: SurfPerch
models.task: Reef soundscape embedding model for few-shot acoustic event classification.
models.input: Five-second mono reef audio sampled at 32 kHz.
models.output: Embeddings and model logits; train a local head for fish, boats, or other target sounds.
models.compute: Public TensorFlow 2 SavedModel about 101 MB unpacked per Kaggle. Profile local batch inference.
models.access: Google SurfPerch v1 is downloadable on Kaggle.
models.license: Apache 2.0 on the Kaggle model variant. Reef audio has source-specific licenses.
models.benchmark: Compare with Perch 2.0 embeddings using the same samples and label budget. Hold out complete sites and recording days; report macro average precision and event-level false alarms.
models.notes: Account for reef training overlap. Transfer to an OOI deep-ocean soundscape requires independent annotation.

models.name: Google multispecies whale acoustic model
models.task: Score supported whale vocalizations in passive acoustic recordings.
models.input: Five-second sliding windows of 24 kHz mono PCM and a chosen hop.
models.output: 12 scores covering seven species-level classes and five call-type classes.
models.compute: TF2 EfficientNet-B0 SavedModel, about 28 MB unpacked per Kaggle. Propose CPU baseline and GPU throughput comparison.
models.access: Downloadable Google model on Kaggle, TensorFlow2/default v2.
models.license: Apache 2.0 on the Kaggle model variant. Recording licenses vary.
models.benchmark: Where the label set overlaps, compare its native scores to Perch/SurfPerch probes on independent deployments. Evaluate event precision/recall and false alarms/hour. BioDCASE 2026 Task 2 has annotated Antarctic whale call timing.
models.notes: Keep the native classifier and a fitted embedding probe as distinct experiments. Some NOAA data were used in development. BioDCASE task rules and domain https://biodcase.github.io/challenge2026/task2

models.name: OceanGPT-basic-4B-Instruct
models.task: Domain-specific language baseline for ocean science questions and event summaries.
models.input: Text questions and optional supplied or retrieved evidence passages.
models.output: Natural-language answers for expert scoring.
models.compute: Qwen-based 4B checkpoint. Propose single L40S inference with fixed context and measured memory and latency.
models.access: Public two-shard Safetensors release, plus larger 30B-A3B alternatives published by ZJUNLP.
models.license: MIT on the selected checkpoint card. Supplied documents retain their own rights.
models.benchmark: Use the authors’ OceanBench for background QA, then identical held-out OOI evidence packets for domain and frontier models. Score units, numerics, citation support, and justified abstentions.
models.notes: The public demonstration may use additional knowledge augmentation. Basic is a text model; image interpretation belongs to the separate OceanGPT-o release.

models.name: OceanGPT-o-7B
models.task: Describe selected sonar or ocean-science images in natural language.
models.input: A rendered image and a question, with the checkpoint’s multimodal processor.
models.output: Natural-language interpretation of image features.
models.compute: Authors recommend a GPU with at least 24 GB VRAM; propose a single-image L40S run before batching.
models.access: Public Qwen-based multimodal release with four Safetensors weight shards.
models.license: MIT on the checkpoint card. Check original sonar and scientific image rights separately.
models.benchmark: Separate image QA track. Use withheld expert-annotated imagery and matched evidence for a vision-capable comparator. Score observable facts, invented features, and abstention on unfamiliar images.
models.notes: The authors explicitly limit sonar support to certain image types. This is text interpretation of images; raw acoustic time-series decoding, quantitative bathymetry and general sonar detection are unvalidated.

models.name: General frontier model with retrieval (OpenAI Responses API)
models.task: Reference system for source-grounded marine QA and automated event reports.
models.input: Question, frozen evidence passages and code-computed measurements. For a distinct image experiment supply the same images to a vision-capable version.
models.output: Generated answer, claim/source references and optionally schema-constrained fields.
models.compute: Hosted API; no local inference GPU required. Pin the available model snapshot, record token usage, cost and latency.
models.access: Hosted service; authenticated API access, proprietary weights.
models.license: OpenAI API service terms apply. Retrieval corpus and supplied imagery keep their original licenses.
models.benchmark: Run a fixed-context generation test against OceanGPT and Qwen using identical evidence. Evaluate retrieval separately with annotated relevant passages, and blind expert graders to model identity.
models.notes: Include missing-evidence prompts. File search provides keyword and semantic retrieval. A citation is evidence only when it actually supports the individual claim.

models.name: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4
models.task: Generate evidence-grounded reports from text or images.
models.input: Study question, frozen measurements, retrieved source passages and optionally image crops.
models.output: Text response to grade for numerical accuracy, citation support and justified abstention.
models.compute: 22.74 GiB of published weights. Proposed L40S trial at batch one and a 4,096-token cap. Peak VRAM, including cache and workspace, remains unmeasured in this project.
models.access: Official quantized checkpoint from Qwen.
models.license: Apache-2.0 checkpoint. Source material in the evidence packet has its own terms.
models.benchmark: Give the same evidence and questions to OceanGPT and a hosted model. Blind reviewers to model identity. Assess multimodal questions separately.
models.notes: Planned Pioneer reporting trial. Model weights count 35B total parameters, with roughly 3B active per token.
